title: Year 4 Number Sentences: Addition and Subtraction
seo_title: Year 4 Addition and Subtraction Number Sentences Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Find unknown values in numerical equations involving addition and subtraction, using the properties of numbers and operations
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction number sentences, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4A01): fact families, missing numbers like ? + 245 = 600 and 700 − ? = 325, properties, the equals sign as a balance and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To find a missing number, use the inverse: subtraction undoes addition, and addition undoes subtraction.
body_html:
Addition and subtraction are inverses

Subtraction undoes addition, and addition undoes subtraction. So three numbers like 245, 355 and 600 make a fact family of four facts.

AdditionSubtraction
245 + 355 = 600600 − 245 = 355
355 + 245 = 600600 − 355 = 245

In a subtraction fact the whole, the biggest number, always comes first.

Find the unknown: use the inverse

A number sentence can have a missing number, shown as ? or a box. Use the inverse operation to find it, then put it back in to check.

Number sentenceDo thisAnswer
? + 245 = 600600 − 245355
700 − ? = 325700 − 325375
? − 148 = 375375 + 148523
Example

? − 148 = 375

The unknown is the number you start with. Undo − 148 by adding: 375 + 148 = 523. Check: 523 − 148 = 375.

Answer: 523

Use the properties

PropertyWhat it saysExample
Commutative (turn-around)You can add two numbers in any order38 + 245 = 245 + 38
AssociativeWith three numbers, you can add any pair first46 + 27 + 54 = 100 + 27 = 127

Subtraction is not commutative: 50 − 20 = 30, but 20 − 50 is not 30. With more than one subtraction, work from left to right.

Example

198 + 245 = 200 + ?

198 + 2 = 200, so take 2 from 245. 198 + 245 = 200 + 243.

Answer: 243

The equals sign means “the same as”

= does not mean “the answer is”. It means both sides have the same value, like a balance.

Example

45 + 38 = 40 + ?

40 is 5 less than 45, so ? must be 5 more than 38: ? = 43. Check: 40 + 43 = 83 = 45 + 38.

Answer: 43

Example

72 − 28 = 74 − ?

72 − 28 = 44. So 74 − ? = 44, and ? = 30. Both numbers went up by 2, so the difference stays the same.

Answer: 30

faq.q: What is a number sentence in Year 4 maths?
faq.a: A number sentence uses numbers, operation signs and an equals sign, like 245 + 355 = 600. In Year 4 (AC9M4A01), students find unknown values in number sentences such as ? + 245 = 600 or 700 − ? = 325.

faq.q: How do you find the missing number in a subtraction number sentence?
faq.a: Use the inverse. For ? − 148 = 375, add: 375 + 148 = 523. For 700 − ? = 325, subtract: 700 − 325 = 375. Then put the answer back in to check.

faq.q: What does the equals sign mean in Year 4?
faq.a: The equals sign means “is the same as”, not “the answer is”. In 45 + 38 = 40 + ?, both sides must have the same value, so ? = 43, not 83.

faq.q: What are the commutative and associative properties of addition?
faq.a: Commutative means you can add two numbers in any order (38 + 245 = 245 + 38). Associative means you can add three numbers in any pairs (46 + 27 + 54 = 100 + 27). Subtraction does not have these properties.

items.e: Subtraction undoes addition. 36 + 47 = 83, so 83 − 36 = 47. Not 119: that adds again instead of using the inverse.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?

items.q: The pans balance, so 45 + 38 = 40 + ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 45 + 38 = 83. So 40 + ? = 83 and ? = 43. Or: 40 is 5 less than 45, so ? must be 5 more than 38. Not 83: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 33: that changes 38 the wrong way.

items.e: Number sentence: 600 − 356 = ?. 356 + 244 = 600 is in the same fact family as 600 − 356 = 244, so 244 students. Not 956: that adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: A cricket club sells 2600 tickets in December. By the end of January it has sold 4350 tickets in total. How many tickets did it sell in January?
items.e: Number sentence: 2600 + ? = 4350. ? = 4350 − 2600 = 1750 tickets. Check: 2600 + 1750 = 4350. Not 6950: that adds the two numbers.
